Definition: a primary verb; properly, to "lay" forth, i.e. (figuratively) relate (in words (usually of systematic or set discourse; whereas G2036 and G5346 generally refer to an individual expression or speech respectively; while G4483 is properly to break silence merely, and G2980 means an extended or random harangue)); by implication, to mean:--ask, bid, boast, call, describe, give out, name, put forth, say(-ing, on), shew, speak, tell, utter.
BiblicalUsage: légō means to say, to speak, and the Bible uses it the way ordinary people use ordinary words — for everything. In Matthew 5:18, "For verily I say unto you"; and in John 8:12, "I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness". In Romans 3:19, "Now we know that what things soever the law saith"; and in 1 Corinthians 1:10, "that ye all speak the same thing".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe every word of Christ carries the weight of the One who speaks — His words do not suggest, they settle. I hold that when Scripture says God says, the discussion is over and the obeying begins. My position is that I will build my life on what He has said, not on what I feel about it.
